title: Diwali Muhurat Trading 2026 Set for Nov 8, 2:20 to 3:30 PM
excerpt: NSE and BSE will hold the special Diwali session on Sunday, November 8, 2026, in the afternoon, opening Samvat 2083 with block deals from 1:50 PM IST and post-close trading to 4:00 PM IST.
body:
• NSE and BSE will hold Diwali Muhurat Trading on Sunday, November 8, 2026, for Laxmi Pujan, with normal trading from 2:20 PM to 3:30 PM IST — an afternoon session this year, not the usual evening slot.
  • The full schedule starts earlier: block deals run 1:50–2:05 PM IST and the pre-open runs 2:05–2:20 PM IST, while post-close trading ends at 4:00 PM IST and trade modifications close at 4:15 PM IST.
  • The session opens Samvat 2083, the new year in the traditional Hindu calendar followed by Indian markets, and all trades executed carry normal settlement obligations.
  • For diaspora investors: the window is 3:50–5:00 AM ET / 12:50–2:00 AM PT on Sunday, November 8 — place any token order through your broker ahead of the 2:05 PM IST pre-open, and do not treat a one-hour festive session as an investment strategy.

India's stock exchanges will open for a special Diwali Muhurat Trading session on Sunday, November 8, 2026, with normal trading from 2:20 PM to 3:30 PM IST, according to circulars issued by the exchanges on October 19. The National Stock Exchange (NSE) and the BSE will conduct the live session on account of Diwali Laxmi Pujan, even though November 8 is a Sunday trading holiday.

Muhurat sessions are often held in the evening, but the 2026 session is in the afternoon. The exchanges laid out a detailed timetable, as reported in the full Muhurat schedule published after the circular and in IANS reporting of the NSE announcement.

The Full Schedule for November 8

The day begins before the main session. A block deal session runs from 1:50 PM to 2:05 PM IST. The pre-open then runs from 2:05 PM to 2:15 PM for order entry, modification and cancellation, with a limit-orders-only window from 2:10 PM to 2:15 PM. Order matching and trade confirmation follow from 2:15 PM to 2:17 PM, and a buffer period runs to 2:20 PM, when normal trading begins.

Normal trading closes at 3:15 PM for securities in the Closing Auction Session (CAS) and at 3:30 PM for non-CAS securities. Non-CAS order matching and trade confirmation run from 3:30 PM to 3:35 PM, followed by a CAS transition period from 3:35 PM to 3:50 PM and a post-close session from 3:50 PM to 4:00 PM. A special pre-open for IPOs and relisted securities runs from 2:05 PM to 2:50 PM, and those stocks trade in the normal market from 3:05 PM to 3:30 PM. The call auction session for illiquid securities runs from 2:25 PM to 3:10 PM. The NSE said all trades executed during the session will result in settlement obligations, as on a regular trading day.

Why Markets Open on a Holiday

Muhurat Trading is a long-standing market tradition held each Diwali to mark the start of a new Samvat year. This year it opens Samvat 2083. The word muhurat refers to an auspicious time, and many traders and investors treat a first trade in the session as a symbolic way to begin the year, often after Laxmi Pujan at their desks.

The practice is decades old. Reporting on the announcement notes that the BSE began Muhurat Trading in 1957 and the NSE adopted it in 1992, after the exchange was founded.

What the Session Does and Does Not Do

The trades are real, but the session is short and liquidity is typically thinner than on a normal day, when the equity market runs for more than six hours. Prices can move on small volumes, and a festive close higher in past years is not a forecast. IANS noted the exchanges will apply system-driven random closure in the final minutes of key order-entry windows, and order entry, modification and cancellation are available only in the designated periods and under the rules for limit and market orders.

Recent history has been positive without being predictive: the Nifty 50 gained 0.10% in the 2025 Muhurat session, 0.41% in 2024 and 0.52% in 2023 — one-hour moves, not evidence about the year ahead.

For NRI and Diaspora Investors

For investors in the United States, the practical constraint is the clock. A 2:20 PM start in Mumbai is 3:50 AM on the East Coast and 12:50 AM on the West Coast on Sunday, November 8. Anyone planning a token purchase should confirm in advance whether their broker or NRI trading account accepts orders for the special session, check the position-limit and collateral cut-offs with that broker, and use a limit order rather than chasing a thin opening print. If you miss the hour, regular trading resumes on the next trading day — missing a ritual session carries no financial penalty.

The more useful Diwali exercise is administrative: review demat nominations and SIP mandates while markets are quiet, and keep any Muhurat trade small and deliberate.
